ctx.x: And then you moved to Dallas?

No, from Greenville we moved to Waco. We thought Waco was... about you know...talking/ Waco was like going to Heaven. Now, I'll tell you something, Danny, and this is a fact. Do you know that I was thirty years of age, and I was getting around in fast circles, before I realized that Jerusalem was not in Heaven. I was thirty years of age, and a friend of mine, Arthur Reid, who was a public speaker here in New York City, called it to my attention, that the church used Land to teach; if to go into Beulah/ you would…

that if I wanted to go to Jerusalem, I would have to buy thing a ticket to Jerusalem. And, it's a funny/ when you say that, you know...that's there's a lot of people that thought to go to Jerusalem, you know,........to cross the River Jordan, you have to go to Heaven. But then we... when I was four...we moved to Dallas, to Waco. And this is when we moved into a little subdivision of Waco, called West Station. West Station was maybe four or five miles out of the city. And, when the time came for us to make this…
